name: Technique - Growl comb and variation
description: Standalone technique from the growl checklist: different wavetables, disperser, notch and comb filters, small smooth moves and resampling.

manual.instruction: Audition several growl wavetables and keep the ones that respond well to the existing LFO and filter movement.
manual.verify: The table changes the character without requiring a new modulation setup.
manual.why: Oddprophet treats wavetable choice as a major part of making a growl unique.

manual.instruction: Add a disperser or diffuser, then try notch filters. Keep the notches narrow enough that the bass still has body.
manual.verify: The growl gains a distinctive phasey texture while retaining weight.
manual.why: Oddprophet uses a disperser/diffuser and notch filters in the variation stage.

manual.instruction: Add a comb filter with the resonator turned up. Move it in small, smooth strokes; large jumps sound broken.
manual.verify: The comb adds a controlled metallic vowel rather than a ringing artifact.
manual.why: Oddprophet recommends raising the comb resonator and making small smooth movements.

manual.instruction: Resample the best variation and compare it with the original at matched loudness. Keep only the version that still reads as the same growl.
manual.verify: The variation is distinct but still usable in the same drop.
manual.why: The checklist's final stage is deliberate variation through multiple passes, not endless knob turning.

notes: Sources: oddprophet, 'I Made A 1-2-3 Method For Dubstep Sound Design...' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OwQDpCtbNTM); Dripment, '2 TEAROUT Serum 2 BASS ROUTINES' (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRfK34KZIf8). Transcript summaries, not quotes.
